title: A London apartment burned down in 2024 and left more than 80 people homeless
summary_full: Residents of London are still obligated to pay mortgages on homes that were ruined by fire, despite the complexities in the ongoing legal struggles involving insurers and administrators. The building's freeholder has gone into administration following the destruction. Consequently, residents are stuck facing demands for unpaid service charges relative to properties that no longer exist, intensifying pressure on the government regarding building safety and restitution for the affected individuals.
